Brand book

One connection. A million travel experiences, matched to every customer.

Bridgify, part of HBX Group, is the infrastructure behind travel experiences. This book holds the brand as it is built today: how it speaks, how it looks and how it moves, on every screen.

01 · Brand and voice

The partner's brand comes first.

Everything Bridgify says comes back to one page of messages. If a line feels unclear, check it against these.

What we are

The infrastructure behind travel experiences. Bridgify, part of HBX Group.

How we describe ourselves

The world's leading B2B travel experiences infrastructure. A B2B traveltech company.

Never "platform" or "aggregator" when describing Bridgify.

What it means

One integration lets a brand sell 1M+ tours, attractions, activities and events in 180+ countries in its own channels, matched to each customer. Bridgify runs the supply, distribution and personalization. The brand keeps the customer.

Four capabilities

  1. 01AggregateThe largest experiences catalog available through a single integration: the major marketplaces, aggregators and direct suppliers. Keep the suppliers you know, add the rest.
  2. 02NormalizeEvery source mapped and de-duplicated into one schema. One integration instead of one per supplier.
  3. 03DistributeInto the partner's own channels, under the partner's brand. Bookings, payments, currencies and fulfillment handled. The partner owns the customer.
  4. 04PersonalizeAIyelet matches the right experience to the right traveler, using intent and context, inside the partner's product.

Proof we can use

1M+experiences
180+countries
1integration
3xthe conversion of standard travel marketplaces

White-Label Marketplace only, always marked with an asterisk: 3% average conversion · $280 average order value · 3 tickets per order on average.

Voice

Short, direct sentences. Numbers instead of adjectives. The partner's brand comes first. No hype words, no em dashes.

  • American English. Short declarative sentences, a period at the end of headings (not list headings such as "Who we work with").
  • The customer is at the centre: "your customers", "your brand", "your product". Bridgify is the infrastructure behind.
  • Figures always carry a short label, and a source when they belong to one product.
  • Never invent numbers, clients, logos, quotes, pricing, team members or URLs. Demos are labelled "Illustrative product preview".
  • Copy v4 is the only source of text.

Two-part headlines

A statement, then a turn. The turn takes the coral ink. The ink goes on the words that carry the customer's benefit, never on the brand name. One heading, one accent.

  • Your customers already book experiences. Just not with you.
  • Don't give travelers a library. Give them the right book.
  • Three products. One connected layer.
  • Built for brands that already have the traveler

Say it like this

Do

One integration. 1M+ experiences in 180+ countries.

Don't

A huge, world-class catalog of amazing experiences.

Adjectives where a number should be.

Do

The B2B travel experiences infrastructure behind your app.

Don't

Bridgify is a travel experiences platform.

"Platform" and "aggregator" are never used for Bridgify.

Do

Your customers book. Your brand stays in front.

Don't

Bridgify: the future of travel, today.

Hype, and the brand in front of the customer.

Calls to action

  • Main: Book a demo ↗
  • Product: How the Experiences API works ↗
  • Text link: Meet AIyelet ↗, Experiences for OTAs ↗
  • Always ↗, after the label. No ↘, →, or arrow square.

Who it's for

Brands that already have the traveler: OTAs and travel platforms, airlines, loyalty programs, banks and card issuers, travel technology companies, hotels, super apps.

Not for travelers looking to book a tour (they find us inside our partners' apps), or tour operators looking for a reservation system.

06 · Shape and material

Soft glass on a warm floor.

Four radii, one for buttons. Quiet cards carry no shadow. Glass is reserved for featured panels and the frames around illustrations. No solid coral frames anywhere.

Quiet card

Lists and grids of equal items.

Radius 18 · 1px quiet line · no shadow.

Glass card

Featured panels and illustration frames.

Peach edge · rim light top and bottom · soft shadow · no outer glow.

Glass over imagery

Only here does the glass blur what is behind it (12px).

Glow

Reserved. One featured element per screen at most, for example a hero visual. Not part of the glass recipe.

07 · Photography

Warm light, inside the product.

Warm travel photos, sunset or evening light, shown inside mockups and product images: experience cards, phone screens, store pages. They show what a traveler would book.

Where photos go

Do
ColosseumAttraction

Inside a product mockup, with rounded corners and live text beside it.

Don't
Full-bleed background

Not as a full background for a section.

Don't

No collages.

Don't

No blue or cold grading, globes, satellites or stars.

Photos: serve WebP or AVIF with a JPEG fallback, at 1x and 2x of the largest size they are shown at; lazy-load below the first screen. Every image needs alt text from Copy v4; decorative images get an empty alt.

08 · Illustration

The content draws the picture.

Before drawing, write in one sentence what the visitor needs to understand. Every wire, layer and object has a job in that explanation.

  • CablesCoral, on smooth, directed paths with few turns. They converge into one bar of dots and branch out from it. They never cross text.
  • Data dotsSmall warm-white circles (r≈3) with a coral glow, moving along cables and breathing. Round, never dashes or capsules. No dot sits off a cable.
  • Contact pointsA cream circle with a coral line, only where a cable touches a part.
  • DevicesPhone, laptop and tablet with a glowing coral edge and a dark screen that lights up.
  • Interface mockupsExperience cards with warm travel photos, rounded corners and a coral button.
  • Glass layers and dot gridsTranslucent surfaces in perspective; a fine matrix of dots with a few lit in coral.

Material and light

  • A small side thickness, a narrow lit edge, a contact shadow and a soft reflection.
  • A dark body with a coral edge, or a cream body with a warm shadow.
  • Local light only: no neon, gold or dramatic corner light.
  • Every glass surface sits on an opaque floor.
  • Text inside illustrations (phone screens, diagrams, windows) scales with the art but is never smaller than 10px as seen. If it does not fit, shorten the illustration or show part of it.

Not in the language: a globe by default, blue, satellites or stars, filled or multicolored icons. HTML, SVG and CSS first; text stays live.

09 · Icons

A thin coral line.

1.5px coral 500, round caps and joins. 24px in lists, 32px for features. Every icon carries the light dot: #FFE2C6 fill, 0.5px coral 500 stroke. Click an icon to copy its SVG.

10 · Motion

Every move explains something.

Each sequence has a beginning, a passage and an end, and every message gets time to be read. Only transform and opacity move. No loops that have nothing to do with the message. Under reduced motion everything shows its final state.

Coral ink

Matched to every customer.

5s, loops, linear.

Entrance

Rise 40px (24px on phones) and fade, 0.9s, one block after another. Plays each time it scrolls into view.

Hover
Book a demo ↗
Meet AIyelet ↗

0.3–0.48s, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Hover or focus to try.

Site-wide motion

Every section enters with the scroll on desktop, tablet and phone. It leaves the hero, anything with its own entrance, anything the page animates itself and pinned stories alone. Reduced motion shows everything at once.

On phones

  • Tap targets at least 44px. Buttons are 40px tall with a 44px tap area.
  • At most one filled and one outlined button per group. Buttons in a group share one width.
  • Hero buttons stay short, side by side when the pair fits, otherwise stacked.
  • The hero fills the first screen. Nothing jumps after the first paint.
  • Phones play the same animations as desktop, starting when they come into view.
  • A section pins on scroll only on screens at least 901px wide and 701px tall. Smaller screens get the phone behaviour.

Accessibility

    {{A11Y}}

Focus is always visible: 2px coral 500, 4px offset.

Before a page goes live

Checked at 360 · 390 · 430 · 600 · 768 · 834 · 1024 · 1280 · 1440 · 1920 px.

  1. A1Layout. No horizontal scroll at any width; content starts and ends on the page margin (grid.margin).
  2. A2Layout. Each section matches its pattern on desktop, tablet and phone (Patterns, Pages).
  3. A3Type. Every text uses one of the 13 type roles; nothing outside illustrations is under 12px; body text 16px on every device.
  4. A4Color. Only the colour tokens are used; text meets the contrast listed in Color.
  5. A5Spacing. Space between elements comes only from the spacing tokens, per device.
  6. A6Components. Buttons, links, chips, cards, stepper, tabs, FAQ and icons match Components in every state (rest, hover, focus, pressed, disabled).
  7. A7Buttons. One primary per group; arrows are always ↗; phone buttons 40px with a 44px tap area. Content sections: buttons of one group share one width. Phone heroes: short buttons side by side when they fit, otherwise stacked (B4h); home hero buttons at equal widths, stacked at 359px and below.
  8. A8Motion. Each animation in motion.json behaves as in its viewer on desktop and phone; pinned sections release after the last step; reduced motion is respected.
  9. A9Copy. Every visible text matches Copy v4; no text added or removed on phones.
  10. A10Images. Every image from assets.json is present, sharp at 2x, and has alt text.
  11. A11SEO. Title, description, canonical and structured data match handoff.json for every page; redirects and clean URLs work.
  12. A12Accessibility. Keyboard reaches every control with a visible focus; screen readers read headings in order.
  13. A13Performance. LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1 on a mid-range phone; no layout jump on load.
  14. A14Browsers. Checked in Safari on iPhone, Chrome on Android, and Chrome, Safari and Firefox on desktop.
  15. A15Header menu. A hamburger is in the header at every width up to 1023px on every page (40px on phones, 44px on tablets) and opens the full menu; no hamburger from 1024px. Check it again after any change to tablet-menu.css or the phone layer.
  16. A16Entrance. Every section except the hero enters with the scroll on desktop, tablet and phone, and none stays hidden after a full scroll to the end of the page.
  17. A17Layers. scripts/sync-mobile.py --check and scripts/sync-footer.py --check pass, and nothing in mobile/ or wide/ was edited by hand.

  --color-coral-300: #FFB194;
  --color-coral-ink-dark: linear-gradient(90deg, #F46649 0%, #FF967B 23%, #FFE2C6 43%, #F88B72 60%, #F46649 78%, #FFB49A 100%);
  --color-coral-ink-light: linear-gradient(90deg, #CF3F25 0%, #E5573A 30%, #E8603F 50%, #D9482C 72%, #CF3F25 100%);
  --color-coral-button: linear-gradient(105deg, #FF9862, #F46649);
  --color-state-success: #63D99A;
  --color-state-warning: #E3B25C;
  --color-state-error: #E07A6A;

  --color-line-on-light: rgba(24,15,16,0.15);
  --font-display: Chillax, sans-serif;
  --font-text: "Sofia Sans", sans-serif;
  --font-code: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace;
  --radius-sm: 12px;
  --radius-md: 18px;
  --radius-lg: 30px;
  --radius-pill: 999px;
  --radius-button: 10px;
  --shadow-none: none;
  --shadow-soft: 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
  --shadow-glow: 0 0 46px rgba(244,102,73,0.2), 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
  --glass-background: radial-gradient(at 100% 0%, rgba(255,137,98,0.18), transparent 30%), radial-gradient(at 0% 100%, rgba(255,120,83,0.17), transparent 26%), linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255,248,241,0.05), transparent 40%, rgba(255,248,241,0.03)), rgba(20,13,11,0.95);
  --glass-border: 1px solid rgba(246,200,181,0.58);
  --glass-inner: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255,241,218,0.58), inset 0 -1px 1px rgba(255,153,123,0.46);
  --glass-blur: blur(12px);
  --content-max: 1560px;
  --illustration-text-min: 10px;
  --margin: max(clamp(40px, 4vw, 64px), (100vw - 1560px) / 2);
  --space-section-y: 96px;
  --space-hero-top: 80px;
  --space-gap-label-title: 24px;
  --space-gap-title-text: 32px;
  --space-gap-title-sub: 8px;
  --space-gap-text-text: 16px;
  --space-gap-text-more: 8px;

  --space-gap-actions-inner: 16px;
  --space-gap-to-link: 24px;
  --space-gap-to-control: 48px;
  --space-gap-control-content: 32px;
  --space-gap-to-content: 64px;
  --space-gap-to-visual: 64px;
  --space-gap-to-foot: 32px;
  --space-card-gap: 32px;
  --space-card-pad: 32px;
  --type-hero-size: clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 60px);
  --type-hero-weight: 300;
  --type-section-size: clamp(36px, 3vw, 44px);
  --type-section-weight: 300;
  --type-section-sm-size: clamp(28px, 2.2vw, 32px);
  --type-section-sm-weight: 300;
  --type-card-size: clamp(24px, 1.9vw, 28px);
  --type-card-weight: 300;
  --type-small-head-size: 20px;
  --type-small-head-weight: 300;
  --type-stat-size: 43px;
  --type-stat-weight: 500;
  --type-body-size: 16px;
  --type-body-weight: 400;
  --type-small-size: 14px;
  --type-small-weight: 400;
  --type-cta-size: 16px;
  --type-cta-weight: 550;
  --type-eyebrow-size: 12px;
  --type-eyebrow-weight: 550;
  --type-nav-size: 12px;
  --type-nav-weight: 550;
  --type-index-size: 13px;
  --type-index-weight: 600;
  --type-caption-size: 12px;
  --type-caption-weight: 400;
  --type-hero-line-height: 1.16;
  --type-hero-letter-spacing: -0.025em;
  --type-section-line-height: 1.2;
  --type-section-letter-spacing: -0.025em;
  --type-section-sm-line-height: 1.2;
  --type-section-sm-letter-spacing: -0.02em;
  --type-card-line-height: 1.25;
  --type-card-letter-spacing: -0.02em;
  --type-small-head-line-height: 1.35;
  --type-small-head-letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  --type-stat-line-height: 1;
  --type-stat-letter-spacing: -0.02em;
  --type-body-line-height: 1.55;
  --type-body-letter-spacing: 0;
  --type-small-line-height: 1.5;
  --type-small-letter-spacing: 0;
  --type-cta-line-height: 1.25;
  --type-cta-letter-spacing: 0;
  --type-eyebrow-line-height: 1.4;
  --type-eyebrow-letter-spacing: 0.15em;
  --type-nav-line-height: 1.3;
  --type-nav-letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  --type-index-line-height: 1.3;
  --type-index-letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  --type-caption-line-height: 1.4;
  --type-caption-letter-spacing: 0;
}
